page: UpCloud PREMIUM-4xCPU-32GB is a memory-optimized virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz. The configuration includes 4 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core under a shared CPU allocation model. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core, alongside 200 GB of local SSD storage and one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core scores reaching 3844.87 and single-threaded gzip compression processing at 41.08 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 14373.65 and a PassMark CPU score of 12350.42, placing it in the average tier. Memory bandwidth is stable, yielding 103.01 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 47.08 GB/sec for write operations. However, the shared CPU allocation limits its capability for heavy multi-threaded workloads, as evidenced by weaker performance in medium-model LLM inference tasks.

From a resource density perspective, this server offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it a cost-efficient option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require dedicated CPU pinning. The combination of 32 GB of RAM and 200 GB of local SSD storage makes it suitable for hosting databases, caching layers, web serving, and general-purpose applications with moderate, bursty computational demands.
